title: Enzyme Kinetics Explorer
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Biology
description: Interactive MicroSim for exploring Michaelis-Menten kinetics and inhibitor effects

learningObjectives: Calculate reaction velocity using the Michaelis-Menten equation for any substrate concentration
Identify Vmax and Km on a velocity vs. substrate curve and relate their biological meaning
Compare competitive versus noncompetitive inhibitor effects on Km and Vmax
prerequisites: Can read and interpret coordinate graphs

keyQuestions: At what substrate concentration does the velocity reach half of Vmax?
How do inhibitor overlays change the curve's shape and why?
What experimental evidence distinguishes affinity changes from catalytic efficiency changes?
commonMisconceptions: Competitive inhibitors lower Vmax rather than shifting Km
Increasing substrate indefinitely always recovers noncompetitive inhibition
Km is interpreted as a rate instead of a concentration
assessmentOpportunities: Students capture probe readings that demonstrate saturation versus low substrate conditions
Learners explain screenshots of each inhibitor overlay and summarize the kinetic shift
Exit ticket asking when a therapy should target Km versus Vmax changes
